items.headline: Product Management & Strategy Leader | Hardware–Software & AI-Enabled Systems | Ex-CEO/CTO & Founder (acquired) | MEMS, Semiconductor, Precision Timing, Navigation
items.about:
I’m a product management and strategy leader with 15+ years building and launching precision electronic systems that blend hardware, embedded firmware, and software tools for AI, navigation, and semiconductor applications. 

I founded and led ePack (acquired by Bliley Technologies), developing high‑yield wafer‑level vacuum packaging for MEMS, securing over $8M in SBIR and commercial funding, and partnering to launch new timing products into customer systems. At SiTime, I led the Michigan site and cross‑functional teams delivering MEMS‑based precision oscillators and ovenized timing solutions used in AI and GPS navigation. 

I now help startups and technology companies turn complex hardware–software capabilities into clear product strategies, positioning, and roadmaps. For my next role, I’m targeting product management and product strategy positions on hybrid hardware–software or AI‑enabled products, ideally where I can own roadmap, customer discovery, and go‑to‑market with strong engineering partners.

items.headline: AI & Blockchain Architect | Helping FinTech Founders & CTOs Scale Payments, Compliance & DeFi Infrastructure
items.about:
Most products don't fail because of bad ideas. They fail because the architecture can't support growth.

I help fintech founders, CTOs, and Web3 teams build scalable AI and blockchain products designed for real-world adoption not just launch day.

What I solve:
→ Tokenization and stablecoin infrastructure
→ Cross-chain and DeFi architecture
→ AI pipelines for fraud, compliance, and payments
→ Production-ready systems that survive scale

I work best with founders and product teams who need more than development support. They need technical clarity, scalable architecture, and execution that can keep up with growth.

If you are building in fintech, payments, DeFi, tokenization, or digital asset infrastructure, send me a message. I am always open to discussing ambitious products and solving hard technical problems.

publications.title: FoG Computing based Wireless Sensor Network for Explosive Material Detection and Security Alert System (e-DASS)
publications.publishedAt: ArXiv, Electrical Engineering and Systems Science > Signal Processing, Cornell University · Jan 8, 2020
publications.description: The terrorism rate in Pakistan becomes higher even after the advancement of information technology. Especially APS Attack and numerous other in different part of country. The root cause of such attacks as according to our research is as: terrorists utilizing the benefit of lack of a full proof security check system. Traditional explosive detection systems are large in size, expensive and require manual attention. These systems are not much useful due to its public visibility intruder or terrorists can easily bypass the system using another route. This term paper is mainly focusing on explosive material detection using IoT with WSN. Explosive Material Detection and security alert system (e-DASS) consists of several hundreds of nodes depending upon the geographical area we are going to cover. Each node should be able to communicate with the other node and update the information if necessary. Tracking of the target can be done in an easier and faster way because all the nodes are synchronized. (e-DASS) is a power efficient explosive detection system. Most of the times nodes will be in the idle state, unless and until positive presence of an explosive is found.

publications.title: An extended quantum process algebra (eQPAlg) approach for distributed quantum systems
publications.publishedAt: Computer Science > Logic in Computer Science, Cornell University · Jan 6, 2020
publications.description: In this work, we have expounded the communication procedure of quantum systems by means of process algebra. The main objective of our research effort is to formally represent the communication between distributed quantum systems. In this new proposed communication model we have ameliorated the existing rules of Lalire's quantum process algebra QPAlg. We have brought some important modification in QPAlg by introducing the concept of formally specifying the Quantum teleportation protocol. We have further introduced the formal description of protocol by using programs that best explains its working and satisfies the specification. Examples have been provided to describe the working of the improved algebra that formally explain the sending and receiving of both classical as well as quantum data, keeping in mind the principal features of quantum mechanics.
